zid000001.name: Dose-response
zid000001.notes: Response (% of maximum) to two agonists, triplicates at 11 concentrations. Simulated with a Hill slope of 1.4. A global fit shares the Hill slope between the two curves; a second fit compares the variable-slope model with a slope fixed at 1 (extra sum-of-squares F test and AICc).

zid000009.name: Does LogEC50 differ between the agonists?

zid000010.name: ELISA standard curve
zid000010.notes: Optical density of IL-6 standards (duplicates; X is log10 of the concentration) and, below them, five samples with an OD but no X. The four-parameter fit interpolates each sample replicate (with a CI) into a result table; a Transform of that table turns log concentrations back into pg/mL. Simulated: the samples' true concentrations are 22, 48, 110, 260, 480 pg/mL.

zid000018.name: BCA protein assay
zid000018.notes: Absorbance of BSA standards (duplicates) and three lysates below them (Y, no X), read off a straight line. Simulated: the lysates contain 180, 620, 1240 µg/mL.

zid000023.name: Enzyme inhibition
zid000023.notes: Initial velocity at seven substrate concentrations with 0, 2, 5 or 10 µM inhibitor. Each data set’s title is its inhibitor concentration: the competitive inhibition model reads it as the data set constant I and fits Vmax, Km and Ki globally. Simulated with Vmax = 120, Km = 6 µM, Ki = 3 µM.

zid000035.name: Photobleaching
zid000035.notes: Fluorescence decaying to a plateau while the baseline drifts upwards. Fit with a user-defined equation, Y = Plateau + Span*exp(-K*X) + Drift*X, from initial values. Simulated with Plateau = 200, Span = 800, K = 0.12, Drift = 1.5.

zid000040.name: Binding with an outlier
zid000040.notes: Specific binding (cpm) of a radioligand, triplicates. One replicate at 12 nM was planted as an outlier (45% low). The fit uses ROUT (Q = 1%) to find and remove it, and shows a residual plot, the runs test and a normality test of the residuals. Simulated with Bmax = 1800, Kd = 4 nM.

zid000048.name: Drug clearance
zid000048.notes: Plasma concentration after a bolus, triplicates. Simulated with a constant 8% CV, so the scatter grows with Y: a one-phase decay weighted by 1/Y², with the test for appropriate weighting (a large P value: the weighting suits the data) and Hougaard’s skewness of the weighted fit.

zid000053.name: Treatment switch
zid000053.notes: A tumour volume index rising until about day 7 and falling after a treatment switch, the two phases overlapping on days 5–7. Simulated lines crossing at day 7, volume 20. “Two intersecting lines” fits one line per data set sharing the crossing point (Xcross, Ycross).

zid000057.name: Two lines: crossing point and slopes

zid000060.name: Uptake and background
zid000060.notes: Transport of a substrate (saturable, Michaelis-Menten) and nonspecific background (linear), duplicates. Simulated. One analysis fits a different equation to each data set.

zid000067.name: Two assays
zid000067.notes: The same 25 samples measured by two assays with similar imprecision. Simulated with a 5% proportional difference. Deming regression (X and Y equally uncertain) rather than ordinary regression, which assumes X is exact.

zid000072.name: Lethality
zid000072.notes: 48 animals, 16 doses (three animals each); Y is 1 when the animal died. Simulated with an LD50 of 2.3 mg/kg. Simple logistic regression gives X at 50% (the LD50) and the fitted probability curve.

zid000079.name: Glucose trace
zid000079.notes: A continuous glucose monitor reading every 30 minutes. Simulated with two meal peaks. A medium LOWESS curve shows the trend without a model.

zid000085.name: Tracer first pass
zid000085.notes: Indicator concentration after a bolus, every 1.5 s. The gamma-variate model is a user-defined equation using the gamma() function: Y = A·X^(B−1)·exp(−X/C)/(gamma(B)·C^B), with A the area under the curve. Simulated with A = 800, B = 3.5, C = 3 s.

zid000090.name: Substrate depletion
zid000090.notes: Substrate remaining (µM) while an enzyme consumes it, duplicates every 4 minutes. The Michaelis-Menten rate law is fit as a differential equation, Y′ = −Vmax·Y/(Km + Y), starting from the parameter Y[0] at X = 0. Simulated with S0 = 100 µM, Vmax = 3 µM/min, Km = 20 µM.

zid000095.name: Antagonist shifts
zid000095.notes: Agonist concentration-response curves (X is the molar concentration, not its log) with a competitive antagonist at 0, 10 nM, 100 nM and 1 µM: the column titles are the antagonist concentrations. “Gaddum/Schild EC50 shift, X is concentration” fits all four curves at once, B taken from the titles (a data set constant), to find pA2 and the Schild slope. Simulated with EC50 = 10 nM and pA2 = 8.

zid000106.name: [Agonist] vs. response, each curve on its own

zid000109.name: Monte Carlo: power of an unpaired t test
